question: None shared. P-158's 95% is the accuracy for Alzheimer's dementia vs non-AD speakers on ADReSS (DementiaBank Pitt Cookie Theft recordings), from acoustic features. P-6's 85.16% is for MCI vs normal cognition in I-CONECT (68 adults aged 75+), from transcripts of conversational video-chat interviews. The channel is shared (speech or language), but the comparison is not: dementia against controls is a different contrast from MCI against controls. P-158's second set (MUDC, 60 Turkish dementia-clinic patients) is also described as CN and AD patients labelled 'dementia or not'. P-158 reports no MCI vs NC result.
metric: Both accuracy, but for different diagnostic contrasts: AD vs non-AD against MCI vs NC.

figures.P-158: ADReSS random forest 95% (+-0.07) by 10-fold CV over speed-perturbed 20-s segments: 1,520 augmented samples from 153 recordings, split at segment level. On the ADReSS held-out test set the accuracy is 73% (the paper gives 48 test recordings in one place and 60 in another). Wilson 95% for 0.95 at recording level (n = 153): [0.903, 0.975]. Wilson for 0.73, n = 48: z^2/n = 0.080; centre = (0.73 + 0.040)/1.080 = 0.713; half-width = 1.96*sqrt(0.73*0.27/48 + 3.8416/(4*48^2))/1.080 = 0.122; interval [0.591, 0.835]. At n = 60 the interval is [0.606, 0.826].
figures.P-6: I-CONECT transformer on ASR transcripts, subject-level 5-fold CV on 68 subjects (34 MCI / 34 NC): accuracy 85.16% (fold SD 5.76), AUC 84.75% (fold SD 5.97); mean AUC over 25 repeated fold configurations 79.94%. Wilson 95% for 0.8516, n = 68: z^2/n = 0.0565; centre = (0.8516 + 0.0282)/1.0565 = 0.833; half-width = 1.96*sqrt(0.8516*0.1484/68 + 3.8416/(4*68^2))/1.0565 = 0.0843; interval [0.748, 0.917].

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists. P-158 has no MCI vs NC contrast and P-6 has no dementia contrast. As arithmetic only: the recorded 95% lies outside P-6's interval, but it is a segment-level CV estimate on augmented copies of the same recordings. P-158's own held-out test accuracy (73%) runs the other way: it lies below P-6's interval, while 85.16% lies outside P-158's test interval by 0.02 (n = 48) or 0.03 (n = 60). So the direction of any 'gap' depends on which P-158 figure is taken.
performance_validity: The exclusion is not met on its letter (95% < 0.97). But P-158's 95% comes from cross-validation over speed-perturbed segments, where copies of one recording can fall in both training and test folds. Its held-out test figure is 73%, so the 95% is not a subject-level estimate. P-6 (85.16%, subject-level CV on 68) passes. Checked against P-158 Tables 4-5 and P-6 Table 3.
reason: The ledger labels both figures 'T1' (MCI detection), but P-158's 95% separates Alzheimer's dementia from non-AD speakers on ADReSS, while P-6's 85.16% separates MCI from normal cognition. That is a misreading (condition 6), and on the printed figures the two papers answer different questions (condition 1). The shared speech channel does not make them comparable. P-158's 95% is also a segment-level CV estimate on augmented data whose held-out counterpart is 73%.
